# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 8

**1** When she had finished, she asked, "Is there anything more you want to know?" I said, "Lady, why is the tower built upon water?" She replied, "Because your life has been saved and will be saved through water. But the tower is founded on the word of the almighty and glorious Name, and it is upheld by the invisible power of the Lord." **2** "That is wonderful, lady. But who are the six young men building it?" "These are the holy angels of God who were created first, to whom the Lord delivered all his creation to build up, increase, and govern. Through them the building of the tower will be completed." **3** "And the other people who bring the stones?" "These too are holy angels of God, but the six have authority over them. When the building is complete, all will celebrate together around the tower and glorify God, because the tower is finished." **4** I asked, "Lady, I want to understand the rejected stones near the tower, those thrown far away, and the cracked ones." **5** She replied: "The stones rejected near the tower are those who have sinned and wish to repent. Because of this they have not been thrown far away — they will be useful if they repent. **6** Those who do repent will be strong in the building and will be incorporated — if they repent now while the tower is still under construction. When the tower is completed there will be no more room, and they will be cast aside." **7** "The cracked ones are those who have faith but also worldly wealth. When tribulation comes, they deny the Lord because of their riches and business dealings." "When will they be useful, then, lady?" "When their misleading wealth has been stripped away, they will be useful to God. A round stone cannot become square unless it is cut and loses something of itself; in the same way the wealthy cannot be useful to God unless their riches are taken away." **8** "I also want to know about the white round stones that did not fit the building — who are they?" She replied, "How long will you be slow to understand, asking about everything yet grasping nothing? These are those who have faith but also hold the riches of this age. When tribulation comes, they deny their Lord because of their wealth and their business dealings."

---

*LOGOS note: The round-stone-must-be-cut metaphor is the Shepherd's sharpest statement on wealth: the wealthy cannot be shaped for God's purposes without loss. This is a significant anti-wealth theology.*
